text: A part such as a motor or gripper that turns the controller's decisions into physical motion. These parts include the motors or cylinders that turn electrical, hydraulic or pneumatic energy into motion.

evidence.quote: the motors or cylinders that turn electrical, hydraulic or pneumatic energy into motion

text: The small play in a gear train that lets the output move slightly without the input moving. Robot reducers keep this play to about an arc-minute or less.
A system that guides the cable carrier to prevent cable loops in the robot work area. For example, a pneumatic retraction system gives adjustable pull-back force using a pressure control valve.

evidence.quote: A pneumatic retraction system provides adjustable pull-back force using a pressure control valve

text: The central component in ros2_control that manages controller lifecycles. It connects the controllers to hardware-abstraction interfaces to run the main control loop.
An industrial Ethernet ring topology with an active ring supervisor that transmits beacon frames. On copper with default beacon settings, it achieves a worst-case recovery time of 2890 µs.
A camera setup in which the camera is mounted on the robot's gripper and moves with it. This lets it look at many places in the cell and move closer to a part to see more detail.

evidence.quote: it can look at many places in the cell and move closer to a part to see more detail

text: An MTC stage that creates robot states on its own without needing a neighboring stage's result. It produces states such as the current state or a set of candidate grasp poses.

Time-critical connected communications in EtherNet/IP that transport I/O data using UDP without embedded protocol headers. Both endpoints already know the meaning, length, and internal offset of every byte in the data exchange.

evidence.quote: Both endpoints already know the meaning, length, and internal offset of every byte in the data exchange

text: A condition where an integrator accumulates excessive error while the actuator is saturated. This causes severe overshoot and delay when the actuator desaturates.
A lithium polymer rechargeable battery common in mobile robots for its high energy density. Battery University gives about 3.6 V nominal per cell, and hobby packs are often labeled slightly higher.
A ros2_control stand-in for a real robot that simply copies each command into its state. This lets software be tested with no robot and no physics.
A joint move in which all joints move together to reach a target, so the tool usually does not travel in a straight line. This instruction is written as MoveJ in ABB RAPID.
A method that controls a machine tool's motion with numbers stored on a medium. Developed for machine tools in the 1950s, it forms a bridge between punched cards and robot programs.
The company that gives professional stewardship, maintenance, development, and support services across the Nav2 and ROS community. Nav2 is the navigation project for mobile robots in ROS 2.

evidence.quote: leading project maintenance, development, and support services across the Nav2 and ROS community
Nav2 is the navigation project for mobile robots in ROS 2.

text: A set of data points in 3D Cartesian coordinates representing physical external surfaces sampled by depth sensors. Before these spatial points can guide a robot manipulator, the raw point cloud must be cleaned up with a library such as the Point Cloud Library (PCL).

evidence.quote: Before these spatial points can guide a robot manipulator, the raw point cloud must be cleaned up with a library such as the Point Cloud Library (PCL).

text: A readable, high-level programming language widely used in robotics for scripting, testing, and higher-level logic. It is also one of the two main languages used with ROS.
Maintenance done after equipment has failed or stopped. Manufacturing establishments relying most heavily on reactive maintenance experience 3.3 times more downtime than those relying on it least.

evidence.quote: Manufacturing establishments relying most heavily on reactive maintenance experience 3.3 times more downtime than those relying on it least.

text: The ROS document that names the coordinate frames mobile robots use, such as map, odom and base_link. Nav2 describes it as defining the frames and conventions required for navigation.

evidence.quote: defining the frames and conventions required for navigation

text: The official bridge suite that translates messages between Gazebo multi-physics simulation transport and ROS 2 publish-subscribe topics. Gazebo does not talk to other programs through ROS itself and has its own messaging system called Gazebo Transport.

evidence.quote: Gazebo does not talk to other programs through ROS itself. It has its own messaging system, called Gazebo Transport

text: A two-way communication pattern in ROS where a client node sends a request to a server node and waits for a response. It is used for quick one-off tasks.
The method of Simultaneous Localization and Mapping, which a mobile robot uses to build a map of an unknown room. At the same time, the robot tracks its own location inside it.
A robot wrist whose last three joint axes meet at one point. This design lets inverse kinematics split into a position part and an orientation part.

Teleoperation software that captures user input from a keyboard, joystick, or gamepad and publishes motion velocity commands. In Turtlesim, the turtle stops if no new velocity command has arrived for one second.

evidence.quote: the turtle stops if no new velocity command has arrived for one second

text: The working point of the tool that the robot positions and moves. It is defined as a point such as the tip of a welding wire or the center between gripper fingers. On ABB robots, the default tool0 has its TCP at the mounting flange.
A motion plan in which an axis speeds up at constant acceleration and cruises at its maximum speed. It then slows down at the same rate, so its speed-time graph is a trapezoid.

The Python-like text scripting language that runs on Universal Robots controllers for motion, I/O, and real-time threads. On the e-Series, the RuntimeMachine communicates with the robot at 500 Hz, a 2 ms frame.

evidence.quote: On the e-Series, the RuntimeMachine communicates with the robot at 500 Hz, a 2 ms frame.

text: The Windows Subsystem for Linux version 2 is a Windows tool that runs a real Linux kernel. It lets developers install Ubuntu and run ROS tools directly on Windows.
How robot programs are organized using RAPID modules and routines, alongside URScript functions and threads. How they recover from errors such as a missed pick, with a 3 by 3 palletizing loop.
The full math of a planar two-link arm covering forward kinematics and the reachable ring. It details closed-form inverse kinematics with atan2, rounding edge cases, and the Jacobian singularity.

Build a ROS 2 camera pipeline in Python using sensor_msgs/Image and CameraInfo, optical frames, image_transport, cv_bridge conversion, and real-time OpenCV edge processing. The pipeline runs without a camera using cam2image test images.

Capstone project: build an open-source ROS 2 cell monitor using stand-in servers. It reads robot state, packed Modbus handshake bits and a camera check, while keeping a maintenance log. The project ends with a real pull request, with no hardware needed.
